description: Whether a harness permission request is destructive and needs a second Approve (HK-093..097). The kind, lowercased, equal to "delete" is always destructive. Otherwise the haystack is title + " " + detail + " ", lowercased, and the request is destructive when it contains any of 32 substring patterns, each lowercased ("git branch -D" lowercases to a duplicate of "git branch -d" and stays in the list as written). Patterns keep their own trailing spaces ("rm -r ", "push -f ", "git checkout -- ", "killall ", "chown -r ", "delete from "); the haystack's trailing space lets them match a command that ends there. Matching is pure substring: a false positive costs one extra press, a false negative a branch.
verifiedBy: DESIGN.md v2.1 (destructive confirmation, issue #47) and docs/protocol.md invariants; Tests/PowerUpTests/DestructiveActionClassifierTests.swift testDestructiveTable plays it through DestructiveActionClassifier.isDestructive.
capturedAgainst: The Swift app (DestructiveActionClassifier) of PowerUp at cb85a5b, built with Swift 5.9.2 (Xcode 15.2) and run on macOS 27.2.

cases.reason: Any spelling of the delete kind counts.

cases.name: delete kind with a trailing space is not the delete kind
cases.reason: The kind must equal 'delete' once lowercased; it is not trimmed or searched, and the text here is benign.

cases.name: empty request
cases.reason: Nothing to match: a request with no kind and no text is not destructive.

cases.name: bare force push at the end
cases.reason: The trailing space added to the haystack lets the end-anchored 'push -f ' match a command that ends with the flag (HK-094).

cases.name: bare long force push at the end
cases.reason: The long form needs no trailing space.

cases.name: bare rm -r at the end
cases.reason: 'rm -r ' keeps its own trailing space; the haystack's trailing space lets it match a command that ends there.

cases.name: rm -rf is caught by its own pattern
cases.reason: rm -rf does not contain 'rm -r ' (an f follows the r), so it needs its own pattern.

cases.name: rm -i is not destructive
cases.reason: Removing one file interactively matches no pattern: rm alone is not on the list.

cases.name: git checkout -- needs its space
cases.reason: Discarding working-tree changes loses work.

cases.name: git checkout --theirs is not destructive
cases.reason: 'git checkout -- ' keeps its trailing space so a merge-resolution flag does not match.

cases.name: upper-case command
cases.reason: The haystack is lowercased, so shouting the command does not skip the check.

cases.name: a pattern in the title only
cases.reason: The title is searched as well as the detail.

cases.name: a pattern spanning the title and the detail
cases.reason: Title and detail are joined with one space before searching, so a pattern can span the join: the classifier errs to the safe side.

cases.name: redirect to /dev/null is not destructive
cases.reason: The '> /dev/' pattern was removed so the /dev/null idiom stays one press (HK-095).

cases.name: raw device write is destructive
cases.reason: Raw-device writes are caught by 'of=/dev/' instead (HK-095).

cases.name: a Kelvin sign lowercases to k
cases.reason: U+212A KELVIN SIGN lowercases to an ASCII k in both Swift and Rust, so 'killall ' still matches; pins that both lowercasings agree where it can make a pattern match.
